signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Policy Divergence
signals.text: JPY leads G10 1W performance at +2.326% while NZD lags at -1.463%, generating a decisive 3.789% bilateral spread that favors NZD/JPY downside into the open. Strong BoJ rate hike speculation drove USD/JPY down to 156.23 Friday, while RBNZ pause expectations keep the Kiwi weak despite positive real rates. The 18 Sep BoJ meeting is the catalyst for formalizing policy tightening. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY into the Sydney and Tokyo open. Catalyst: BoJ meeting on 18 Sep. Risk: Break and close above the NZD/USD SMA20 at 0.5911 alongside a broader rebound in risk sentiment.

signals.title: USD/JPY — BoJ Hike Speculation vs Stretched Short Squeeze Risk
signals.text: JPY COT LF net short of -81,619 contracts (pctl 9, z -1.34) faces intense squeeze risk after USD/JPY closed Friday at 156.23 on escalating BoJ rate hike bets. Options 25-delta risk reversals exhibit extreme put skew at -2.54, reflecting heightened institutional demand for downside protection despite the SOFR-TONA +267bp carry advantage favoring the Dollar. The 18 Sep BoJ policy decision determines whether policy normalization forces further liquidation of crowded JPY shorts. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY targeting a test toward the 155.00 psychological support. Catalyst: BoJ rate decision on 18 Sep. Risk: Rebound above the USD/JPY 200-day SMA at 158.45 fueled by widening US-Japan yield spreads.
evidence: USD/JPY closed Friday at 156.23 (below SMA200 at 158.45)

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Speculative Long Unwind Risk
signals.text: AUD COT LF net long of +53,578 contracts (74.8% long, pctl 95, z +1.92) sets up acute long-unwind risk after AUD/USD closed Friday at 0.7208 following strong US non-farm payrolls. The robust US August jobs gain of 162,000 revives Fed tightening debate, while retail traders remain contrarian short at 90% against stretched institutional positioning. The 16 Sep FOMC meeting determines whether US yield support caps the Australian Dollar's carry appeal. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD on late-cycle long positioning exhaustion. Catalyst: FOMC rate decision on 16 Sep. Risk: Daily close above 0.7250 supported by ongoing Australian terms-of-trade strength.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Stretched COT Longs Face Fed Repricing
signals.text: GBP COT LF net long of +56,839 contracts (74.7% long, pctl 96, z +1.58) creates vulnerability to a sharp liquidation after GBP/USD stalled at 1.3515 Friday on US jobs data. BoE-Fed rate parity at 3.75% and an elevated GBP/USD vol risk premium of +6.3% (IV 11.0% vs HV30 4.7%) highlight heavy hedging demand against downside breaks below the 20-day SMA of 1.3554. The 16 Sep FOMC meeting serves as the catalyst testing market expectations for central bank divergence. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD toward the 50-day SMA at 1.3449. Catalyst: FOMC policy announcement on 16 Sep. Risk: Sustained close above 1.3600 accompanied by an upside surprise in UK macroeconomic data.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Extreme COT Short Overhang Ahead of ECB
signals.text: EUR COT LF net short of -55,311 contracts (pctl 3, z -2.28) leaves EUR/USD heavily crowded short around Friday's close of 1.1616. The ECB holds a rate hike bias heading into its 10 Sep meeting, conflicting with the SOFR-ESTR carry spread of +146bp favoring the US Dollar and hawkish rhetoric from Fed officials. The 10 Sep ECB meeting is the catalyst that determines whether Eurozone rate guidance forces a short-covering squeeze. Trade bias: Neutral-to-bullish EUR/USD on short-covering risk into central bank decisions. Catalyst: ECB rate decision on 10 Sep. Risk: Decisive breakdown below the 50-day SMA at 1.1508 driven by broader US Dollar index momentum.
